classification: Diagnostic CPU/allocation cost of an isolated optional ACK ownership policy; no production adoption or throughput acceptance.
common_work: A borrowed real52-byte pure ACK passes through provider receiveTransferWithRecovery, actual SendPack admission and terminal consumption. Before uses the existing provider shard; after uses the existing dedicated ACK producer directly.
context_controls: After-only Available and Wait isolate context composition. The Wait callback forces one initial refusal then success and includes every join/cancel cleanup; it does not measure host wait duration.
interpretation: The no-pressure path adds no per-item context join. Actual refusal pays one correctly cancellable join. The recovery owner is allocated once per existing flow worker; item layout costs32additionalbytes. The admission timing change includes the intentional worker-route change and is not an isolated interface-boxing measurement.
limits: No physical A/B/A calibration or SDK throughput conclusion follows from these microbenchmarks.
matched_fixture: Common admission benchmark body is byte-identical. A variant-only factory creates once the corresponding production recovery value outside timed work.
results: Admission before2368–2936ns/op and after1305–1357ns/op; both880B/op16allocs/op. providerReturnItem grows304→336bytes. Available context11.58–12.04ns/op,0B/0allocs/0joins; forced-wait context312.2–315.1ns/op,248B/5allocs/1join.
run_context: Both benchmark processes overlapped on a loaded Apple M1 Max host. Absolute timing and timing ratios are diagnostic only; no quiescence wait or performance acceptance claim.
source_pair: Corresponding optional ACK-owner v3 before/after; after also includes hard caller-isolation guards. Same experimental receiver-service sampler in both.
